rows.42:00f0:
All six stories were over.
But there was still no sign at all of the seventh person coming.
There was no point waiting any longer.
I stood up and gave my closing remarks.
"Well then, everyone.
Thank you all so much for tod..."
Just then, the door suddenly flew open.{p}
rows.42:0200:
"Hey!"
We all jumped out of our skins.
After a whole evening of scary stories, a sudden visitor made our hearts skip a beat.
In the doorway stood a man, his eyebrows raised in anger.{p}
rows.42:02c4:
"Mr. Kuroki!"
Hosoda suddenly stood up.
...So this was a teacher Hosoda knew.
"What do you kids think you're doing?!
It's already past nine o'clock!"
rows.42:039c: Mr. Kuroki was so overpowering that everyone in the room got to their feet.{p}
rows.42:03e8:
"...What were you doing?"
Mr. Kuroki looked around at all of us, then his eyes stopped on me, and he asked in a voice that was quiet, yet heavy and forceful.
"...Uh, well, we're doing a special feature on scary stories for the next school paper, so..."
"Go home."
Without letting me finish, Mr. Kuroki herded us toward the door.
We hurried to clean up, then rushed straight out of the newspaper club room.{p}
rows.42:0530:
"Honestly, staying this late..."
The teacher grumbled and complained, then clicked his tongue.
We were in for an incredible scolding.
We lined up in a row outside the club room, hunching our heads down into our shoulders.
"That's enough for today.
We'll talk tomorrow. Now get yourselves home."
"Yes, sir!"
We practically fled for home.
The teacher followed us all the way to the school gate.
It wasn't to see us off, not at all. It was to make sure we really headed home.{p}
rows.42:06d8:
We hurried home.
The Seven Mysteries had turned into Six Mysteries, but it couldn't be helped.
It was the seventh one's fault for standing us up and never showing.
Tomorrow I'd have to explain properly to Hino what had happened.
Worse, tomorrow the teacher was sure to chew us out something awful.
I really didn't want that.
My feet felt heavy all the way home.{p}
rows.42:0800:
...The teacher stood in front of the school gate until every one of them was out of sight, making certain they had gone home.
Once they were gone, he let out a long sigh, then clicked his tongue again and again.
"...Unbelievable.
I thought nobody was left.
And the damn kids were still hanging around."
Muttering like that, the teacher went back through the deserted school at night to the night-duty room.{p}
rows.42:0950: When he opened the door of the night-duty room, a choking stench of blood spread through the air.{p}
rows.42:09b4:
No wonder.
On the floor of the night-duty room lay a corpse he had killed just a little while ago, a kitchen knife still plunged into its back.
"Man, I wondered what I'd do if they found out.
On full-moon nights, I get this uncontrollable craving to kill people.
I'd finally bagged a nice piece of prey, and my fit had died down, too.
...Well now. All that's left is figuring out how to dispose of this one."
The teacher stood at the kitchenette and began fixing a late supper.{p}All the while gazing at the corpse that should have been the seventh one, licking his lips hungrily...{p}
